subject: Clarify: what Redwood stores by default — prompts vs outputs vs ephemeral caches
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightloop.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightloop.com
Date: Fri, 9 Aug 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q: what exactly you retain by default (prompts vs outputs vs caches)

Hi Karthik —

We're doing a short security assessment ahead of our pilot and need a concise clarification of Redwood's default data retention behavior. The two areas that keep coming up on our end:

1) What do you define as "prompts" vs "outputs" in your telemetry? Do you store both by default for hosted API customers?
2) Are transient runtime artifacts (KV cache, prefix cache, intermediate tokens used for streaming) ever written to durable storage? If so, for how long?
3) If a customer needs a full purge for a specific workspace/namespace, what is the request path and expected SLAs?

Could you reply with short, actionable bullets we can include in our questionnaire? Ideally by EOD Monday — appreciate it.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Security Lead, BrightLoop

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightloop.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 9 Aug 2029 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what exactly you retain by default (prompts vs outputs vs caches)

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear questions. Below are concise bullets you can copy into your questionnaire. I kept the language short and factual. If you want, Marissa and I can put these into a short mutual action plan (attached) and jump on a 30m call next week.

- Prompts (customer-sent request payloads): stored by default for Hosted API customers as part of request/response logs. These are retained for 45 days by default unless the customer is on an Enterprise plan with a custom retention policy.
- Outputs (model responses/completions): stored alongside requests as response artifacts; default retention is the same 45-day window.
- Prompt derivatives (embeddings, indexing artifacts created by customer-initiated jobs): treated as customer-created artifacts and retained per the artifact type; by default embeddings created via the hosted embeddings endpoint are retained for 90 days unless otherwise configured.
- Runtime caches (in-memory KV cache, prefix cache, intermediate streaming token state): never written to durable storage in the Hosted runtime. These are ephemeral and expire when the request finishes or when the serving instance is recycled.
- Logs and telemetry (request metadata, trace ids, route decisions): minimal telemetry is retained for 90 days to support debugging and SLOs; it does not contain full prompt/output payloads unless required for investigation and authorized by the customer.
- Customer-requested purge: customers open a support ticket (Support > Data Actions) or use the enterprise purge API (link below). Standard purge SLA for Hosted customers: 72 business hours for workspace-level purges; for Enterprise private deployments we offer on-premise purge assistance and certified evidence.

Attachments: I've attached an initial MAP that outlines timelines and the DocuSign step if you want a contractual amendment. Marissa will add the part about contractual SLAs below.

Cheers,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightloop.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 08:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what exactly you retain by default (prompts vs outputs vs caches)

Alyssa —

Adding a few contract-level clarifications so you can paste into your procurement/security form:

- Default hosted retention = 45 days for prompt/response artifacts. Customers on Dedicated or Private can specify retention policies in their account settings or via the enterprise contract.
- For compliance evidence: we can provide a SOC 2 summary and a scoped log-retention attestation for the pilot (attached).
- When you request a purge, please include the workspace ID and example request ids (if available). Our data actions team will provide a purge confirmation ticket number and an exported certificate of deletion for your records.

If you want tighter controls during your pilot (no retention of prompt/response), we support an "ephemeral mode" configuration for pilot workspaces that prevents storing prompt/response payloads at all; this requires a quick network/ACL change and a signed MSA addendum. We can spin that up before you ingest PII.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightloop.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Aug 2029 11:19:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what exactly you retain by default (prompts vs outputs vs caches)

Hi all —

Quick legal/security confirmation: the statements above are accurate representations of our current Hosted behavior as of Aug 2029. A couple of fine points for BrightLoop's questionnaire:

- "Stored" means placed in our encrypted object store tied to the customer's workspace ID and subject to our default retention window. Access to payloads is logically restricted; we require a documented justification and approval for any manual retrieval.
- Ephemeral mode (no prompt/response persisted) is available for pilots but will remove our ability to do post hoc debugging unless you enable limited diagnostic capture for a signed timeframe.
- For regulated requests (e.g., DSAR/erasure compliance), we coordinate with the customer and provide a deletion log and signed confirmation within the contractual SLA.

I've attached a short SOC2 evidence summary for your security team; happy to review it live if you want.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy — Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@brightloop.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, security@brightloop.com
Date: Sun, 11 Aug 2029 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: what exactly you retain by default (prompts vs outputs vs caches)

Alyssa —

Following up with two quick links you can use in your questionnaire and the MAP attached as promised:

- Short: Hosted default retention = 45 days for prompts/responses; runtime caches are ephemeral and not durably stored; telemetry retention ~90 days.
- If you need zero retention for prompt/response during pilot, request "ephemeral mode" and we'll provision a pilot workspace with no storage for payloads (we'll need an MSA addendum).

Links: https://docs.redwood.ai/platform/retention (public doc)
Drive MAP: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/3AQ2-DataRetention-MAP

Would you like us to schedule a 30m call next Tue (8/13) at 10am PT to walk through the purge steps and provide the deletion certificate template?

Best,
Karthik
